newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Futures Exchange readies to trade new products.
newsitem.headline: HK Futures Exchange readies to trade new products.

text.p: The Hong Kong Futures Exchange Ltd has enhanced its launch pad for new products to enable members to directly access its trading system, senior exchange executives said on Thursday.

"The launch pad for new products has been enhanced with modifications...to the sofware of the (exchange's) automated trading system to allow members to access the system through their own integrated dealing terminals," exchange chairman Frank Wong said prior to the exchange's annual general meeting.
The exchange would launch several new products in 1997, all of which would be traded on the automated system, Wong said.
Electronic trading provided investors with a more transparent, fairer, and efficient market place and was more cost efficient than open outcry trading, Wong said.
The exchange will relaunch trading in futures contracts on the Hong Kong inter-bank offered rate (HIBOR) on September 26.
It also planned to introduce futures and options contracts on additional equity indexes.
"Another index contract will be launched this year," said chief executive Ivers Riley, adding that it would be an index from a market in the Asia region.
He would not say if the exchange would consider launching a futures contract on an index of China-related stocks.
HSI Services Ltd, keeper of the Hang Seng Index, said on Thursday it would launch a new index of China-affiliated stocks on June 16. No details on the make-up of the index have yet been released.
The exchange would also introduce futures contracts on eight additional stocks, bringing the exchange's stock futures product line to a total of 13, said Wong.
"We do not have SFC (Securities and Futures Commission) approval for all eight contracts, but we are close," said Riley.
An energy futures contract with an Asian benchmark was also under study but would not be ready this year, executives said.
The exchange also was not planning its own precious metals contracts.
"We are not going to create our own contracts in precious metals, said Riley. "We are happy that our members have the link with NYMEX (New York Mercantile Exchange)."

The Hong Kong Futures Exchange Ltd will launch its trading partnership with the NYMEX on Friday. The products available for trading in Hong Kong include gold futures, silver futures, copper futures, and platinum futures.

The Hong Kong Futures Exchange's trading volume rose 13.9 percent to 5.9 million contracts in 1996 compared with 1995, and in the first five months of 1997, volume rose 14.8 percent over the corresponding period last year, chairman Wong said.
Volume in Hang Seng Index futures rose to 500,746 contracts in May, an all time monthly volume record, he added.
